name: Liège-Bastogne-Liège
story: A 55-rider breakaway went clear after only a few kilometres, with Remco Evenepoel among the attackers. UAE initially held the gap at around 30 seconds before allowing it to grow to roughly four minutes. After the turn in Bastogne, a headwind gradually reduced the advantage, with UAE and Decathlon driving the peloton. The final attackers were caught with 80 km remaining. On La Redoute, Benoît Cosnefroy led out Tadej Pogačar, whose attack only Paul Seixas could follow. Pogačar dropped him on Roche-aux-Faucons and soloed to a fourth Liège-Bastogne-Liège victory.
